title: The Howard Garrideb advertisement
body: John Garrideb burst into Nathan Garrideb's room waving a newspaper and handed over a marked advertisement. It read: 'HOWARD GARRIDEB, Constructor of Agricultural Machinery. Binders, reapers, steam and hand plows, drills, harrows, farmers' carts, buck-boards, and all other appliances. Estimates for Artesian Wells. Apply Grosvenor Buildings, Aston.' The American said his agent in Birmingham had sent it from a local paper, and he arranged for Nathan, who seldom left his room, to travel there the next afternoon. That evening Watson told Holmes he had noticed that the word 'plough' was misspelt. Holmes replied that it was bad English but good American; that buck-boards were American too; and that artesian wells were commoner in America than in England. It was a typical American advertisement, though it claimed to be from an English firm. Holmes added that he might have warned the old collector that he was going on a wild-goose chase, but thought it better to 'clear the stage' by letting him go.
